newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips hold lofty gains after April PPI boost.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips hold lofty gains after April PPI boost.

text.p: U.S. stocks held strong gains in afternoon trading as investors took heart after a report indicated that wholesale prices declined in April.

The U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI), which had been forecast to come in unchanged, fell 0.6 percent. The "core" PPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, also surprised took Wall Street by surprise with a fall of 0.1 percent. It was forecast to rise 0.1 percent.
The Dow industrials up 45 to 7319 after an earlier jummp of 77 points at the opening. The New York Stock Exchange imposed trading curbs at 0934 EDT/1334 GMT.
Other major U.S. stock indexes were also higher, with the Standard & Poor's 500 Index up 5 to 838, the Nasdaq up two to 1335, and the Russell 2000 index of small cap stocks up one to 365.
The strength in stocks was underpinned by strength in bonds, with the long bond up 16/32, pushing the yield down to 6.88 percent.
Advancing issues beat losers on the New York Stock Exchange by 5 to 3 with volume at about 380 million.
